newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Optus to offer 400 mln shrs - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Optus to offer 400 mln shrs - paper.

text.p: Australian largest private telecommunications firm, Optus Communications, will offer about 400 million shares when it launches public float prospectus next month, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Monday.
"The Herald understands about 400 million shares will be offered in the float," the newspaper said.
"This will be made up of a sell down from the existing institutional investors, the issuing of new shares and about 100 million shares from Mayne Nickless Ltd," the Herald said.

All of the institutional shareholders - Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP), National Mutual and the AIDC - have indicated to the float organisers they are prepared to sell down, the Herald said.

"It is understood Mayne Nickless has decided to provide about 400 million shares to its existing investors through an entitlement issue, leaving 100 million to be placed into the open float," it said.
The remaining stock would come from the issue of new shares through a rights issue to existing Optus shareholders.

"Optus Communications' two international shareholders, BellSouth Corp and Cable and Wireless Plc are almost certain to take up their rights to ensure their stakes of 24.5 percent each are not diluted by the issue of new ordinary shares," the Herald said.
"But Mayne Nickless and the institutional shareholders are not expected to take up the rights, making these shares available for the float," the newspaper said.
A registered prospectus for the public offering is expected to be released in late October.
